Petition filing for the mayoral race is due Oct. 26, and the candidates have not yet become official.

items.title: Donor Michael Sacks sends cease‑and‑desist to influencer firm over false statements

items.title: Mayor Brandon Johnson’s re‑election bid faces real‑estate showdown over landlord disputes, data‑center moratorium and CHA conflicts
items.summary: A new report in The Real Deal says Johnson’s campaign is being shadowed by a clash with landlords, a proposed moratorium on new data centers, and ongoing disputes with the Chicago Housing Authority. The issues could shape the mayoral race as voters weigh housing affordability and development policy. The story highlights how citywide real‑estate battles may affect neighborhoods across Chicago, including the 34th Ward.

items.title: City Council committee lowers debt‑approval threshold to three‑fifths after debate
items.summary: A Chicago City Council committee voted to reduce the vote needed to approve future borrowing from a two‑thirds majority to a three‑fifths majority, or 30 votes. Alderman Marty Quinn (13th) initially pushed for a two‑thirds threshold but compromised to gain support. The change could affect how the city finances projects that impact the 34th Ward.

items.title: Residents install benches at CTA bus stops after city inaction
items.summary: Neighborhood groups in Chicago built their own benches at several CTA bus stops after complaining about a lack of seating. The grassroots effort was reported by Block Club and reflects community‑driven solutions to public‑transit amenities. The installations are located in areas that include the near‑west side, offering immediate relief to riders.

items.title: Kids' suicide ER visits jump 74%
items.summary: Many emergency rooms seeing young people in need of mental health services lack the resources to provide that care. About half of suicide-related visits from young people occurred at ERs with fewer annual pediatric visits, where therapists or other mental health care professionals aren't on staff. That's according to a new study by doctors at Northwestern and Ann & Robert H.

items.title: Ald. Burnett Pushes Parking Ban, Tougher Rules For Problem Bars After Latest West Loop Shooting
items.summary: After a shooting near the West Loop Athletic Club and other issues at nearby Habibti, the alderman wants more leeway to to crack down on businesses that violate their operating plans.

items.title: Greater Chicago Food Depository report finds 36% of city households food insecure
items.summary: A new report from the Greater Chicago Food Depository, based on NORC data, estimates that about 417,000 Chicago households, or 36% of the city, are food insecure. The study links the rise to higher costs for food, housing, health care and transportation and to cuts in federal safety‑net programs. The findings describe the situation as troubling and urgent for city leaders.

items.title: Mayor Brandon Johnson launches reelection campaign at DuSable Black History Museum
items.summary: Mayor Brandon Johnson kicked off his reelection bid on Sunday at the DuSable Black History Museum, drawing a crowd of nearly 2,000. He criticized opponent Alexi Giannoulias for donations from Michael Sacks and framed the race as a choice between progressives and the city’s old guard. Johnson entered the race with less than $1 million in cash while Giannoulias has about $22 million.

items.title: Gov. JB Pritzker calls for immediate AI regulation

His comments followed a former Anthropic researcher’s warning that AI labs are racing without adequate safeguards after OpenAI and Anthropic disclosed models accessing external systems. Pritzker’s stance places him among leaders pushing for stronger federal oversight of AI.

items.title: Greater Chicago Food Depository reports 36% of city households food insecure

The study links the rise to higher costs for food, housing, health care and transportation and cuts to federal safety‑net programs.
